I feel like I've asked this befoe, but I can't find the post, if so.

Super-Scientific Tachyon uses Experiment on a deck that has exactly one card in it.  What happens?

1) Nothing.  (If so, on what reasoning?)

2) The single card is revealed (on the principle of "do as much as you can"), and then:

2a) The revealed card is discarded, because it cleary doesn't share a keyword with <null card>.

2b) The revealed card is returned, because it is nonsensical to compare something with nothing.

2c) The revealed card is put into play, because a <null crad> doesn't *lack* any keywords.  (I don't buy this one myself, but include it for completeness.)

 

I lean towards 2a, myself, but I'd be interested in hearing other arguments and/or offical rulings.

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
I can point at Spiiff's FAQ were it talks about

What causes a deck Reshuffle

2) revealing cards does not trigger a reshuffle. you only reshuffle a
deck when you need to draw a card from it, and revealing cards is not
the same thing as drawing. so if you are triggering an effect which says
to reveal the top five cards of a deck and there are only three cards
in that deck, you may only reveal those three and then you’re done.
[br]and

Searching decks/revealing cards

Effects which direct you to “reveal” cards are slightly different from effects  which direct you to “search” for a card. When “revealing” cards, you must  pull the cards off the top of the deck in order until you find the card you’re  looking for. When you “search” a deck for a card, you are allowed to  choose which card you want as long as it satisfies the criteria you’re searching  for; you don’t necessarily have to pick the first one you come upon.

W hat if an effect tells you to search the deck/reveal cards until you find a  card and then do something once you’ve found it, but you don’t find the card?

Answer: Nothing.
 
example: plague rat’s “noxious bite” card says to “search the villain deck
for a copy of the card ‘infection’. Put it into play. Shuffle the villain
deck.” If you search the deck for “infection” and there are no infections
in the deck, then just shuffle the deck and proceed with the game.
 
[br]
[br]Which [s]implies[/s] outright states that you reveal when instructed even if you know you can't fulfil the condition.

MigrantP:

… Experiment is written such that two cards are necessary for the power to do anything. It includes instructions on what to do with those exact two cards. If there are not two cards, the power can't work - hence, fizzle.

I agree that the power can't complete, but it can do something – reveal the lone card.  Which, if you don't have your deck memorized, could be quite valuable, even if nothing else happened.

If we take the rule that explicit numbers either complete or fizzle, that leads to a bizarrre situation with Baron Blade.  Baron Blade's flip text says (in part) "All 3 copies of "Mobile Defense Platform" are moved to the villain trash."  What happens if BB flips while one (or more) of the Mobile Defense Platforms is under Savage Mana?  The interpretation above suggests that none of the MDPs would move, since you can't move all 3, and THAT doesn't seem at all right.

(What the app actually does in the BB/SM case seems correct to me: The two non-Mana-ed MDPs go in the trash, while the Mana-ed one stays where it is.  Since it is under another card, it isn't (currently) a "Mobile Defense Platform".)

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
Nah, you're not misremembering it. (I'm not a good judge of crazy, so I'll leave that to others. )

Christopher has always (in the past) said you do as much as you can of an action. You can see this in all these examples of previous rulings.

I can understand why Christopher ruled it differently here, though. This is a very different situation for one reason only: the cards revealed are then compared. In the past, we've never had the revealed cards matter to each other - each could be managed independent of the other. That's not an option here. So Christopher had to come up with something that makes sense.

I do agree that it would be more consistent to say the single card revealed, compared to nothing, and - since it doesn't match - is discarded. But I can understand why this situation is different from past rulings.
